source_text: Mors autem iudicialis transiit in eo, in quo peccaverunt omnes, sed libera voluntate; quo verbo, id est omnes Scripturarum more multitudo, non universitas indicatur.
pass_a_gloss: But judicial death passed in him in whom all sinned, but by a free will; by which word, that is all, by the custom of the Scriptures a multitude, not a universality, is indicated.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5
LS relative; Rom 5:12 in quo omnes peccaverunt — keep Latin force

pass_b_english: The death imposed by judgment passed on because all sinned—but they sinned by free will (Romans 5:12). In keeping with scriptural usage, the word ‘all’ here indicates a multitude, not absolutely everyone.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian: Paul says death passed to all, not sin; distinguish temporal death from eternal punishment.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: Julian takes the Latin in quo causally, “because,” as he explicitly explains in Book 2, section 174; it does not here identify Adam as “the one in whom” all sinned.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
